extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, USPTO management, and other patent stakeholders (e.g., applicants, attorneys, policy analysts)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and metrics used by the USPTO Office of Patent Quality Assurance (OPQA) to evaluate patent examination work products (Office actions) for statutory compliance, clarity, process performance, and stakeholder perception. Includes the sampling and review types OPQA uses and specific metric names/definitions used historically and currently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA reviews work products for statutory compliance standards to produce quality metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory compliance is assessed both to inform quality metrics and to evaluate whether Office actions adhere to the criteria of compliance under each statutory basis. Compliance measurement includes consideration of an Office action's ability to advance prosecution. Reviews include non-final, final, and allowance Office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA assesses Office actions for clarity as part of quality reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity assessments produce granular data used to provide meaningful feedback to Technology Center management and to identify training opportunities. Product indicators explicitly focus on clarity alongside statutory compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA highlights and assesses the use of best practices in fully compliant Office actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since 2018 OPQA emphasizes best practices in accolade letters to examiners; best practices are considered drivers of clarity and correctness and are encouraged through feedback. Best practices are treated separately from mere statutory compliance to promote higher-quality work products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Composite Score (seven individual metrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning in FY2011, OPQA combined seven individual quality metrics into a Quality Composite Score (historical metric).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The seven individual metrics combined were: In-Process Compliance Rate, Final Disposition Compliance Rate, Complete First Action on the Merits Review, First Action on the Merits Search Review, QIR (Quality Index Reporting), External Quality Survey, and Internal Quality Survey. (Note: the composite score was retired in FY2016 in favor of a simplified metrics program.)

rubrics_metrics.name: In-Process Compliance Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: A named metric measuring compliance for in-process Office actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as 'measuring compliance considering an Office action's ability to advance prosecution.' In-process reviews include non-final actions and are intended to assess whether actions appropriately move prosecution forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Disposition Compliance Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: A named metric measuring compliance for final dispositions (allowances and final rejections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also described as 'measuring compliance considering an Office action's ability to advance prosecution.' Final disposition reviews examine whether final office actions meet statutory and procedural standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete First Action on the Merits Review
rubrics_metrics.description: A specific metric reviewing the completeness of the first action on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the historical set of quality measures used to evaluate whether first actions on the merits are complete and meet required standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Action on the Merits Search Review
rubrics_metrics.description: A specific metric reviewing the search quality and completeness in the first action on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses whether the examiner's first action included an adequate prior art search and supporting search rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Index Reporting (QIR)
rubrics_metrics.description: A process-oriented metric capturing average actions per disposal (QIR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QIR is the average of actions per disposal and includes indicators such as RCEs as percent of total disposals; reopenings after final; second-action non-finals; and restrictions after first action. QIR-type data inform process indicators and are used to evaluate efficiency and rework.

rubrics_metrics.name: External Quality Survey
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey-based metric capturing stakeholder perceptions of examination quality from external stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPQA administers external stakeholder quality perception surveys; results are compared to statutory compliance statistics to ensure that perception aligns with measured compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal Quality Survey
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey-based metric capturing internal stakeholder perceptions of examination quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used alongside external surveys and statutory compliance measures to form perception indicators and to identify gaps between perception and measured quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product indicators (FY2016 onward)
rubrics_metrics.description: A category of metrics focused on the quality of Office actions (statutory compliance and clarity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduced with the Quality Metrics Program in FY2016 to simplify reporting. Product indicators emphasize both statutory compliance (adherence to statutory criteria) and best practices/clarity in Office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process indicators (FY2016 onward)
rubrics_metrics.description: A category of metrics focused on process-related performance (QIR-type data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process indicators include measures such as average actions per disposal and related operational metrics that reflect processing behavior and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perception indicators (FY2016 onward)
rubrics_metrics.description: A category of metrics focused on survey-based perception data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perception indicators draw from internal and external quality surveys to capture how stakeholders view examination quality and to compare perception with measured compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Random-sample audit methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA audits a random sample (approximately 10,000 Office actions) of examination work products each fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The random sample is reviewed based on statutory compliance standards to produce quality metrics. Sampling includes non-final, final, and allowance actions to obtain a thorough understanding of work product quality and processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted and special reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA conducts additional review types beyond the random sample to meet Agency objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: reviews of newly hired examiners at the Patent Training Academy to assess training effectiveness; strategic reviews based on data-analysis of examination behaviors to identify improvement areas; and reviews of PCT Written Opinions to ensure contractors produce high-quality work for the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback and data-driven trend analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA provides feedback to Technology Centers and performs trend analysis to identify underlying causes of quality issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The granularity of statutory compliance and clarity assessments facilitates identification of quality trends, training opportunities, evaluation of training effectiveness, and actions to reduce rework and promote efficiency. USPTO statisticians perform trend analysis on statutory compliance and clarity assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of classification and adherence to policy (historical audit focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical Quality Audit Program criteria included statutory compliance, adherence to policy, and accuracy of classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These criteria were part of the program as early as 1967 and reflect enduring evaluation dimensions beyond statutory compliance and clarity.
